title: Payment Methods
story: Your online store needs to accept different payment types — cash, credit cards, and cryptocurrency. Each one has different info: cards have numbers, crypto has coin names.
why: Payment methods showcase enums with varied data — some variants carry one value, others carry different types, all under one unified type.
analogy: Payment types are like different checkout lanes: the cash lane is simple, the card lane needs a card reader, and the crypto lane needs a wallet address. Each lane has different equipment (data).
try_it: Add a `PayPal(email: Str)` variant to the Payment enum. Update both functions to handle it. Test with a PayPal payment.
tips: Use `_` when you don't need the payload value — `CreditCard(_) => "Card"` is cleaner than `CreditCard(number) => "Card"`
Different variants can have different payload types — Cash has none, CreditCard has Str
Name payload fields clearly: `CreditCard(number: Str)` tells you the field holds the card number
common_mistakes: Creating a variant with an unused payload — if a field stores the card number, use it somewhere
Using `_` when you DO need the value — you can't print `_`; name the field if you need the data
Trying to access `payment.number` — payloads are only accessible through match patterns
